context: The input is the integer array nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], with indices 0 through 3, and the target sum is target = 13.

An auxiliary hash table, map, records elements already visited. Each key, labeled “Element,” is an array value. Its associated value, labeled “Index,” is the corresponding array index. On each iteration of a single loop, first check whether the complement target − nums[i] is in map. If so, immediately return [map[target − nums[i]], i]. Only if the complement is absent do we store the current entry nums[i]: i in map.
description: Looking up the complement before storing the current element ensures that its partner comes from a different index before i. Three frames show the decisions and hash table states at i = 0, 1, and 2. The first frame shows the table after inserting 2: 0, rather than the initial empty table.

frames.announcement: Visit 2 at index 0. Its complement, 11, is absent from the hash table, so store the entry 2: 0 in map.
frames.explanation: i = 0 points to 2. The right side explains that 13 − 2 = 11 is absent from the initially empty table, so we insert 2: 0. Now map = {2: 0}. The search has yet to return an answer. Next is 7 at index 1.
frames.key_state: i = 0 (value 2): complement 11 is absent. After insertion, map = {2: 0}.
frames.title: Complement 11 is absent, so record 2

frames.announcement: Visit 7 at index 1. Its complement, 6, is absent from the hash table, so store the entry 7: 1 in map.
frames.explanation: i = 1 points to 7. The right side explains that 13 − 7 = 6 is absent from map, so we insert 7: 1. The table previously contained only key 2. Now map = {2: 0, 7: 1}. The search has yet to return an answer. Next is 11 at index 2.
frames.key_state: i = 1 (value 7): complement 6 is absent. After insertion, map = {2: 0, 7: 1}.
frames.title: Complement 6 is absent, so record 7

frames.announcement: Visit 11 at index 2. Its complement, 2, is in the hash table at index 0, so return [0, 2].
frames.explanation: i = 2 points to 11. The right side explains that 13 − 11 = 2 is in map and map[2] = 0, so we return indices [0, 2]. The table still contains {2: 0, 7: 1}. We skip inserting 11 and finish before reaching 15 at index 3.
frames.key_state: i = 2 (value 11): complement 2 is in map at index 0, so immediately return [0, 2]. The table still contains {2: 0, 7: 1}. We do not insert 11 or process 15.
frames.title: Complement 2 is present, so return the indices

result: Assuming a hash lookup takes O(1) time on average, the whole algorithm takes O(n) time on average and O(n) auxiliary space, trading space for time.
summary: Store previously seen elements and their indices in a hash table. Look up the complement before deciding whether to store the current element.
title: Solving two sum with a hash table
